rows.name: -ub
rows.reason: the chunk BoltBeam's prompt limit picks for this machine (the offload page's prompt setup): the smallest within the policy tie of the best

rows.name: -b
rows.reason: raised to -ub when -ub is larger (the command does it); a prompt is read in chunks of at most -ub, so a -b above -ub adds no larger chunk

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_MMID_PAR_MIN
rows.reason: the patch's crossover (outputs are bit-identical either way); --measure confirms it on this machine. Measured: with the whole Flash-Next model on the card, at 10k the parallel sort cut mm_ids from 82 to 26 ms

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_MMQ_ID_J
rows.reason: a sweep knob, left unset: llama.cpp's own mean-columns rule picks the tile width. Measured: with the whole Flash-Next model on the card, wider tiles read slower (J=128 at -ub 2048: expert MMQ 354 -> 395 ms), and the mean-columns rule was the best of the sweep

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING
rows.reason: on: a reused pinned buffer saves pinning each checkpoint's destination afresh, and the results are bit-identical

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING_MAX_MIB
rows.reason: a cap on pinned memory: a state read larger than it takes the old path

rows.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_MIN_HEAD
rows.reason: stock (0): every expert is on the GPU, where the head batch costs no expert upload; not measured there

rows.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_TAIL_ONLY
rows.reason: off, because the workload is chat (--workload chat, the default): with it on, a follow-up that changes an earlier part of the conversation re-reads the whole prompt; outputs of a single request are identical. Turn it on only for one-shot prompts (--workload one-shot)
